newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut jury convicts ex-fugitive of 1986 rape.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut jury convicts ex-fugitive of 1986 rape.

text.p: Alex Kelly, the former international fugitive who became a symbol of privileged youth in trouble with the law, was convicted on Thursday of raping a 16-year-old girl in a car 11 years ago.
The six-member jury reached its verdict after deliberating half a day each on Wednesday and Thursday. Kelly's first trial ended in a hung jury in November.

Kelly, 30, who had claimed the sex was consensual, exploded in court when the verdict was read. "I'm not guilty! I'm not guilty! I'm serious," he said. Stamford Superior Court Judge Kevin Tierney ordered him to sit down and be quiet.
A bond hearing was set for the afternoon. "The state will argue for a high bond or no bond," an investigator in the state's attorney's office told Reuters.

Before his conviction, Kelly had been free on a bond of $1 million, secured by his parents' house in the blueblood New York suburb of Darien, Connecticut. He was convicted on a single count of sexual assault, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years' imprisonment. Sentencing is expected in about six weeks.

A former high school wrestling star, Kelly fled the United States on the eve of his original scheduled trial in 1987. His eight-year odyssey through 15 countries included time spent on the ski slopes of Europe.

Authorities have said he was financed by his wealthy parents. According to his passport, introduced as evidence, the countries he visited included the Netherlands, Italy, Greece, Egypt, Turkey, the Soviet Union, Tunisia, Morocco, Portugal, Hungary and Denmark.
